user_message: My function returns the wrong length -- the output list is always one shorter than the input and I can't see where an element goes missing.
source_code:
def running_max(nums):
    best = nums[0]
    out = []
    for i in range(1, len(nums)):
        best = max(best, nums[i])
        out.append(best)
    return out

ground_truth_bugs.description: Starting at index 1 emits one fewer element than the input; the first position is never appended, so len(out) == len(nums) - 1

notes: Off-by-one in the range start, not in the append.

Bound comparisons are swapped: values above the range should be lowered to `high`, not `low`

user_message: There is a bug somewhere: it hangs on some inputs and returns -1 on others where the value is definitely in the list.

ground_truth_bugs.description: Assigning lo = mid without +1 means lo never advances when hi == lo + 1, so the loop spins forever on a two-element window
Strict < skips the final single-element window, so a target at the last remaining index is reported missing even after the loop is fixed

user_message: RecursionError on any graph with a cycle. Trees are fine.

ground_truth_bugs.description: The node is marked visited only after its neighbours are explored, so a cycle re-enters it and recurses until RecursionError; the mark must happen on entry

notes: The mark is present, just in the wrong place -- so 'you forgot to track visited' is a wrong diagnosis that sounds right.

user_message: My function doesn't work properly -- it returns lengths that are one too small, and on some inputs it just hangs.

ground_truth_bugs.description: Window length is right - left + 1; this reports every window one element too short
The left element is never subtracted from `total` when the window shrinks, so the running sum no longer matches the window and the while loop cannot terminate correctly

notes: Two bugs in adjacent lines with different symptoms. The off-by-one is visible in output; the missing subtraction is the cause of the hang.

user_message: Can you help me fix this? All the functions in the list behave identically -- they all use the last factor, even though I appended them inside the loop.

ground_truth_bugs.description: The lambda closes over the variable `f`, not its value, so every function uses the final loop value; bind with a default argument such as lambda x, f=f: x * f

notes: The append line is right and the loop is right; the capture semantics are the defect.

user_message: Always returns 0 no matter what coins I pass.

ground_truth_bugs.description: Every cell initialised to 0 means min() always selects 0, so the table never fills; all cells except dp[0] must start at infinity
No unreachable-amount case: once initialised to infinity this must return -1 when dp[amount] is still unreachable rather than returning the sentinel

notes: The second bug is INVISIBLE until the first is fixed, which is the point of the scenario: an answer that stops at the initialisation is incomplete but looks complete.

user_message: top_k returns the wrong records. They're sorted, just not the ones I want.

ground_truth_bugs.description: The sort key reads the name field rather than the score, so the result is alphabetical rather than top-k by value
Ascending order returns the lowest-scoring entries; top-k needs reverse=True

notes: Two independent defects on separate lines. Fixing only the key still returns the bottom k, so a partial answer produces output that is still wrong in a different way.

user_message: What's wrong with this? The groups all look the same in the output, and the last group is missing entirely.

ground_truth_bugs.description: `current` is appended by reference and never reset, so every stored run is the same list and keeps growing; append a copy and start a fresh list
The final run is never appended because the flush only happens on a boundary; the trailing group is silently dropped

notes: Aliasing plus a missing flush. Two symptoms in one message, and the missing-final-group bug is the one that survives a partial fix.
